questions.text: Give the formal definition of the finite automaton, M, shown below. [a four-state automaton over {a, b} with states q1 to q4; diagram in the original paper] Indicate which of the following strings the machine will accept or reject: (i). aab (ii). abb (iii). abab (6mks)

2. Given that Σ = {0,1}, convert this regular expression to NFA: 0(011)* ∪ 1 (5mks)
3. Given that L1 and L2 are regular languages, prove that the languages are closed under union operation. (4mks)

Let G = (V, T, P, S) such that Σ = {0,1} and the set of rules are given below:
X = YY | Z
Y = 0Y | Y0 | 1
Z = 0Z00 | 1
(i). Give the formal definition of G. (2mks) (ii). Describe L(G) in English (1mk) (iii). Give one string G can generate and one string it cannot generate (2mks) (iv). Prove that L(G) is not regular. (5mks)

Convert the following ε - NFA to its equivalent NFA [states A, B and C: A loops on 0, A → B on ε, B loops on 1, B → C on ε, C (accepting) loops on 0, 1; diagram in the original paper]
(i) Find E - closure of each state (3mks).
(ii) Draw E - closure transition for all 0's and 1's in transition table (8mks).
(iii) Draw the transition diagram of the NFA (5mks).
(iv) List and give reason for your accept states (4mks).

(a) Construct NFA which accepts all strings over an alphabet Σ = {0, 1} where giving strings ends with "0, 1". L = {01, 001, 101, 10001 etc.}. (4mks)
(b) Construct NFA with ε and without ε which accepts all strings over alphabet Σ = {a, b, c} which contains multiple a's followed by multiple b's and followed by multiple c's (6mks)
(c) Discuss the tuples notations in ε – NFA (5mks)
(d.) Construct a PDA that accepts the language L = {WCWR} over Σ = {a, b, c} W = (a+b)* (5mks)

(a) Push Down Automata (PDA) is a complement of finite state machine with more memory capacity which makes it more powerful with the stack implementation. Discuss based on its model diagram, stack and tuples with a sample of PDA. (15mks)
(b) Construct a DFA that accepts 01 or a string of at least one "1" followed by 0 over Σ = (0,1) show an instance of trap state in your transition diagram. (5mks)

(a) In a tabular form discuss the following terms: Power of an alphabet, Language, Strings, Alphabet (Σ) and Sigma plus (Σ+). (10mks)
(b) Given: Σ = {a, b}, L = {x∈Σ*|x is a string combination}, write all strings in Σ4. (4mks)
(c) Write the strings that the following DFA will accept (3mks) [diagram in the original paper]
(d) What does the following figure most correctly represents? (2mks) [a single accepting start state F with a loop on x]
(e) Write the strings that will not be accepted by the following DFA? Give one reason for your answer (2mks) [diagram in the original paper]

(b) Explain the following statement: satisfying the pumping lemma (for regular languages) is a necessary condition for a language to be regular language, but not a sufficient condition. Use examples of languages satisfying the pumping lemma where necessary, in order to make your point. (4 marks)

(a) Let the context free grammar G be <VN, {a, b, c}, P, S> where: P = {S → aSb, S → c}. Using G, show derivations of the following strings from S: i. aaacbbb ii. aaaaacbbbbb iii. acb iv. aacbb (2 marks each)
(b) Convert the productions of the following grammars into Greibach Normal Form. i. G = {VN, VT, P, S} where P = { S → aSb, S → ab} ii. G = {VN, VT, P, S} where P = {S → aaSbb, S → c} (4 marks each)
(c) Find a context free grammar that can generate the following language: L = {a^n b^n : n ≥ 1} ∪ {a^n b^2n : n ≥ 1} (4 marks)

(a) Give the state diagram for a deterministic finite state automaton each that recognizes the following languages: I. {w | w does not contain a substring ab}. II. {w | w does not contain a substring baba}. III. {w| w does not contain exactly two a's} IV. {w| w = ε or a} (4 marks each)
(b) From the finite state acceptors, arrived at in 4a(I) and 4a(IV) above, formally, derive regular grammars that can generate the same languages. (2 marks each)

(a) Translate each of the following context free grammar production sets into Backus Naur Form (BNF). i. {S → aSA, bSB, S → C, C → cC, C → ε, A → a, B → b} ii. {S → aSBB, B → b, S → ε} iii. {S → aASB, S → ε, B → b A → a } iv. {S → aAASBB, S → ε A → a, B → b} (2 marks each)
(b) For each of these languages, find a description for each of the languages in (a) i to iv above. (1 mark each)
(c) For each of (a) (i) and (ii), derive non-deterministic pushdown automata that accept the same language as the respective grammar generates. (4 marks each)
